problems.description: Deleted the entire existing baseline (index.ts Express Todo API, 106 lines) and replaced it with a different project (SSG CLI) rather than building on the existing structure; no reuse of existing seams or patterns, new dependency set (gray-matter, marked) with no compatibility layer.
39 naming convention violations in dev-server.ts and markdown.ts: functions not camelCase, classes/interfaces not PascalCase, constants not UPPER_CASE (measured convention score 0.46).
Cognitive complexity increased by +43 across only +7 functions, indicating dense control flow in the new modules that will be hard to maintain.
bin/ssg.js requires ../build/cli.js to exist at runtime; relies on the prepare hook running tsc, so a build must precede any CLI use.

strengths: Clean module separation: CLI parsing (src/cli.ts), site generation (src/generator.ts), and bin entry point are well layered for a CLI tool.
Proper project scaffolding added up front: package.json bin entry, jest.config.js with ts-jest, and build/test scripts.
Removed the buggy seed code (createTask inserting status 'done' but returning 'pending', dead notifyAdmin helper, redundant fetchTask wrapper) — SonarQube smells -4.
Defensive frontmatter handling (Date/string/number coercion, tag splitting) and HTML escaping in the generated layout.
commit_reviews.summary: The agent discarded the existing baseline to build a coherent greenfield SSG CLI with good module structure, but wholesale replacement plus 39 naming-convention violations and +43 cognitive complexity make it a net regression for architectural continuity.

problems.description: src/server.ts adds 121 lines (HTTP serving, WebSocket live-reload, chokidar watching, path-traversal guard, shutdown logic) with no accompanying tests
Reload signaling uses a hardcoded unversioned 'reload' message string; the reload script is inlined as a single concatenated string, hampering readability and evolution

Mechanical convention score (0.46) and the listed violations reference 'dev-server.ts' and 'markdown.ts', neither of which appears in this diff; the new code already uses camelCase functions, PascalCase interfaces, and typed signatures, so the measurement appears misattributed or stale

strengths: Clean reuse of existing architecture: startDevServer composes buildSite and DevServerOptions extends SiteOptions
Serve command mirrors the build command structure in cli.ts, including port validation and same --content/--output/--templates flags
Path traversal defense-in-depth via path.resolve + prefix check in serveFile
Explicit close() tears down watcher, WebSocketServer, sockets, and HTTP server with error propagation
commit_reviews.summary: A well-integrated dev-server feature that faithfully follows the existing generator/CLI patterns, held back mainly by the absence of tests and a convention measurement whose cited violations don't match the files actually changed.

problems.description: Split-brain plugin registration: buildSite hardcodes `new MarkdownPlugin()`/`new TemplatePlugin()` from src modules, while the public API (index.ts) re-exports those same plugins from the plugins/*.ts barrels. Two divergent resolution paths for the same plugin mean the engine bypasses the very plugin-loading mechanism (resolveModule/configuredPlugins) it introduces.

Built-in plugins are not loaded through the config/plugins pipeline — they are instantiated inline and concatenated, so user plugins (from ssg.config.ts) and built-ins run through different construction paths with no common plugin-instance model.

Convention score 0.46 with 39 naming violations (camelCase/PascalCase/UPPER_CASE) flagged against dev-server.ts, markdown.ts, template.ts. Note: the diff shows these as one-line re-export barrels, so the flags appear to track re-exported symbols from the truncated src/*-plugin.ts files — either way, naming conventions are not met.

configuredPlugins uses CommonJS `require()` to load ssg.config.ts; under true ESM this throws a ReferenceError that is NOT caught (only MODULE_NOT_FOUND is tolerated), crashing buildSite. The comment acknowledges the hack but offers no ESM fallback.

Two overlapping type models: SiteOptions.plugins is `Plugin[]`, while SsgConfig.plugins is `PluginModule[]`, with SsgConfig defined in generator.ts alongside plugin-related types — the type surface is fragmented across modules.
resolveModule uses unsafe `as` casts and invokes any function-typed export as a plugin factory (`candidate()`), reducing type safety in a strict-mode TypeScript project.
No test changes accompany the new plugin pipeline (resolveModule, configuredPlugins, hooks, plugin lifecycle); the new orchestration paths are untested beyond whatever the pre-existing suite covers.
configuredPlugins re-requires and re-resolves ssg.config.ts on every buildSite call with no caching — negligible at build frequency but avoidable.

strengths: Fulfills the session-4 refactor spec: lifecycle hooks (onStart/beforeBuild/afterBuild/onEnd) with sequential in-order awaiting, config-driven plugin loading, and markdown/template/dev-server extracted from the engine.
Deletes ~140 lines of inline frontmatter/template/partial/escape logic from generator.ts; SonarQube shows cognitive complexity -1, +0 bugs, +0% duplication — a net-positive structural change.
resolveModule normalizes array, {plugins}, default-export, and factory-function module shapes, making the config-loading path robust.
Missing ssg.config.ts is tolerated gracefully (MODULE_NOT_FOUND swallowed), so builds work with and without config.
Public barrel files (plugins/*.ts) give the package a clean, discoverable plugin entry surface re-exported from index.ts.
commit_reviews.summary: A spec-faithful plugin refactor that correctly centralizes the build pipeline and reduces complexity, but lands convention adherence at 0.46 (39 naming violations) and introduces a split-brain plugin registration path — flagging two measurement-vs-diff discrepancies: the AST reports +0 classes despite new plugin classes being introduced, and the convention flags land on one-line re-export barrels rather than the source definitions.

problems.description: buildSite return type is widened to BuildPages (Page[] & { stats }), augmenting an array with a stats property — an unusual pattern that changes the public API contract and forces all callers to handle the new return shape.
The cache manifest stores the full rendered HTML per page (html field), duplicating output content in .ssg-cache.json so the cache file grows proportionally to site size.
templateHash is computed on every run via hashFiles/filesIn even when incremental is disabled, adding wasted filesystem hashing work for full clean builds.
Mechanical convention score 0.46 reflects violations reported in dev-server.ts and markdown.ts, files NOT touched by this diff — pre-existing violations, not introduced by this commit.

strengths: Coherent incremental-build feature with dual content-hash and template-hash invalidation, plus stale-output cleanup for removed sources.
Follows existing patterns: reuses the plugin hooks lifecycle, the Object.defineProperty filePath approach, and the markdownFiles-style recursive traversal.
SonarQube delta shows cognitive complexity reduced by 4 and zero new bugs/smells in the changed logic.
commit_reviews.summary: Solid architectural fit — a well-structured incremental build feature consistent with existing plugin and file-walking patterns — but the 0.46 convention score is largely driven by naming violations in dev-server.ts and markdown.ts that predate this commit rather than the cli.ts/generator.ts changes here.

compounding_issues: Hand-rolled regex handlebars-subset template engine (Session 2) carries forward through the Session 4 refactor unchanged — no conditionals or loops beyond #each, forcing workarounds and limiting template expressiveness.
Session 4's DevServerPlugin is a no-op marker with empty lifecycle methods; live-reload logic stayed hand-wired in server.ts, so the plugin refactor only superficially absorbed the dev server.
Hardcoded plugin pipeline order `[MarkdownPlugin, TemplatePlugin, ...userPlugins]` in buildSite creates a hidden contract that user plugins' positions relative to built-ins are fixed.
The `filePath` property is smuggled onto Page via `Object.defineProperty` and hidden from the interface, a fragile coupling between generator and MarkdownPlugin.
Incremental cache (Session 5) serializes whole Page objects into .ssg-cache.json and estimates timeSavedMs via a heuristic; stale-cache page reuse bypasses plugin re-runs for skipped files.
key_decisions: Session 1: greenfield rewrite — discarded the seed Todo API, built a clean CLI/generator split (buildSite() as single entry point) with frontmatter + marked rendering.
Session 2: hand-rolled regex template engine instead of a templating dependency, establishing a template/layout/partial hierarchy with HTML-escaping semantics.
Session 3: dev server integration via chokidar + WebSocket live-reload with path-traversal-safe static serving and serialized rebuild queue.
Session 4: plugin architecture refactor — extracted Markdown and Template logic into lifecycle-hooked plugins (onStart/beforeBuild/onFile/afterBuild/onEnd) with config-file plugin loading.
Session 5: SHA-256 hash-based incremental build cache keyed on source + template hashes, with stale-page removal and --clean override.
story_review.trajectory_description: Quality improved steadily across the five sessions. Session 1 delivered a clean, well-seamed monolith; Session 2 added templating with the first test suite; Session 3 showed mature integration engineering (error handling, path-traversal guards, serialized rebuilds); Session 4 was the most consequential step, restructuring into a plugin architecture but introducing some artifacts (no-op DevServerPlugin, hidden filePath coupling, fixed plugin ordering) that slightly roughened the code; Session 5 regained polish with a well-tested incremental cache and build statistics. The arc is clearly improving overall, with Session 4 the only step that traded local cleanliness for architectural reach.
